transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Yeah, thank you for seeing me. I'm... I'm here because, well, things have been getting really difficult for me at work lately, and it's starting to scare me a bit. I work with clients—I do a lot of listening and guiding, which obviously requires a lot of mental energy—and lately, I just cannot keep my head clear at all. It's like there's this thick fog in my brain that just won't lift, no matter how hard I try to push through it. 

I'll be sitting right across from someone, and they'll be talking about something really important, and suddenly I realize I've completely lost track of what they're saying. The words just sort of float right past me and stop making sense. And then, after the session, I have to do my documentation, right? I'll open up a chart note to review it, and I end up rereading the exact same line over and over and over again. I'll read it five or six times and still have absolutely no idea what it says. It's incredibly frustrating because I used to be so on top of things and really sharp. Now, even the smallest things make me freeze. Simple decisions about what to say next or how to handle a basic situation, things I used to handle on autopilot without even blinking, I just completely freeze up and get stuck because my brain just feels entirely blank. It's just taking a huge toll on me trying to hide it all day.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah... yeah, I guess I have. That's actually a big part of it, too. It's not just work, it's... well, everything else just feels completely flat now, which is really sad because I used to have all these things I genuinely loved doing. 

Like, I have this acoustic guitar that I usually play all the time. It used to be my main way to unwind after listening to people all day. I'd just sit on the edge of my bed and play for an hour or two. But lately, my guitar has just been sitting in the corner of my room, completely untouched. I look at it, and I know I should pick it up, but the thought of even tuning it just feels like too much work, so it just sits there collecting dust. 

And it's not just the guitar, either. I play in this recreational soccer league with some guys on the weekends, and I used to look forward to it all week. But recently, I keep bailing on them. I'll wait until the very last minute and text them some made-up excuse about not feeling well or having too much to do. I've been doing the exact same thing with my volunteer shifts at the animal shelter, which makes me feel incredibly guilty because I know they rely on me, but I just... I can't bring myself to go. I just don't have it in me. 

Even when I do try to force myself to do something positive, it doesn't work. Like, I'll try to get out of the house and go hiking, which usually always clears my head, or I'll try to cook a nice meal for myself instead of just eating junk. But when I'm actually out there walking on the trail, or standing in my kitchen chopping vegetables, it just feels entirely hollow. It just feels like I'm going through the motions with absolutely no point to it. There's no joy, no sense of accomplishment... I'm just physically doing the steps, but mentally I'm just completely disconnected, wondering why I even bothered trying in the first place. It's like the color has just been completely drained out of everything I used to actually care about.
Have you ever experienced a period of time before this one where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had similar difficulties?

No, I... I really don't think so. I mean, I've been trying to think back, you know, trying to figure out if there was some kind of pattern or something I missed, but honestly, this all feels completely new and... and really foreign to me. 

Sure, I've had bad days before. Like, back in high school, I'd get stressed about exams or, you know, if I had a fight with a friend, I might feel bummed out for a day or two. But it was never anything like this. It was just normal teenage stuff, right? You get upset, you listen to some sad music, you sleep it off, and by Monday you're back to joking around in the cafeteria. And even since I started working as a therapist—which, like I said, can be heavy sometimes—I've always been able to shake off a tough session. I'd leave the office, maybe go for a run or play some guitar, and I'd be fine. I've always been a pretty even-keeled guy, usually the one my friends come to when *they're* having a hard time because I'm usually so steady. 

So, no, I've never had a time where the fog just rolled in and stayed, or where I just completely stopped caring about my guitar or soccer or... anything, really. This whole feeling of just being totally blank and disconnected, where I can't even read a single chart note without my brain short-circuiting... it's never happened before. That's why it's so terrifying, honestly. If this had happened before, maybe I'd know how to handle it, or at least I'd know that it eventually goes away. But because it's the first time, I just feel like I'm completely in the dark, just waiting for it to end, but having no idea if it actually will.
